newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy sees lower comparable store sales.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy sees lower comparable store sales.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc, one of the nation's largest retailers of electronics, computers and appliances, said on Tuesday it expects comparable store sales to show declines for the next several quarters.
Last week, Best Buy had reported comparable store sales for December fell 13 percent from a year earlier while total sales for the month were off five percent to $1.3 billion.
Best Buy cited continued industry weakness in personal computers and consumer electronics for the lower sales.
Comments on sales expectations were contained in a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The Minneapolis-based company currently has 272 stores, 234 of which were considered comparable in December.

In mid-December, Best Buy had reported fiscal 1997 third quarter comparable store sales fell eight percent from a year earlier. At that time, the company also reported a third quarter loss of about $11 million, its first loss in a decade.

Because of the loss, the company failed to comply with terms of its loan agreement. Later in the month, Best Buy's lenders waived compliance with the terms and revised the requirements through the second quarter of fiscal 1998.

According to the SEC filing, Best Buy intends to work with its banks following the end of its current fiscal year (February 28, 1997) to permanently amend and extend the term of the loan agreement which currently matures in June 1998.

Fiscal third quarter results also caused violations of the terms of two of the company's long term real estate financings, according to the filing. Best Buy is in the process of obtaining a waiver and permanent change to the terms of one of those financings, the filing said. The other financing has also been resolved, it said.
Best Buy said it expects to reach a permanent agreement on these financings after its current fiscal year ends. These agreements mature in September 1998.

Best Buy also said in the filing that it expects cash flow from operations, the company's working capital credit agreement, inventory financing pacts, and customary vendor terms will be sufficient to meet its working capital needs for the next year.
